title: Atrial fibrillation — irregularly irregular tachycardia (USMLE CVS case)

properties.cases overview: 58F with 1 week of lightheadedness and palpitations; anxious, pale, mild diaphoresis; irregularly irregular rhythm; HR 142, BP 118/55 → atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (RVR), symptoms from reduced cardiac output.
properties.feedback:
Key feedback points from our discussion:
- “Irregularly irregular” is a pattern phrase that strongly suggests atrial fibrillation.
- Mechanism of symptoms: RVR shortens diastolic filling time and reduces stroke volume → lightheadedness/diaphoresis.
- ECG anchor: absent organized P waves + irregularly irregular R-R intervals.
- Management framework: first assess hemodynamic stability; if unstable → immediate synchronized cardioversion. If stable → rate control (β-blocker or non-DHP CCB; ± digoxin in select settings) and anticoagulation decision using CHA₂DS₂-VASc; rhythm control considerations depend on duration/TEE and symptoms.
